interactions.label: What is the primary reason the syndromic approach to STD management was develope

params.question: What is the primary reason the syndromic approach to STD management was developed for Indian primary care settings?

answers.text: Organism identification is unavailable or impractical at the point of care

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Syndromic management exists because most patients first seek care where same-day lab results are impossible — cultures are technically demanding, transport media unavailable, and patients cannot return for follow-up.

answers.text: Syndromic treatment uses cheaper antibiotics than targeted therapy

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Cost is not the driving rationale. The approach was designed because organism identification is simply not available at the point of first contact — not because targeted therapy is expensive.

answers.text: Patients prefer receiving treatment without undergoing laboratory tests

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Patient preference is not the reason. The approach exists because laboratory confirmation is unavailable, delayed, or the patient cannot return — it is a systems-level constraint, not a preference-driven choice.

answers.text: Most STDs are caused by a single organism, making identification unnecessary

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is incorrect. Each syndrome can be caused by multiple organisms (e.g., urethral discharge by both N. gonorrhoeae and C. trachomatis), which is precisely why syndromic management treats all probable pathogens of a syndrome at once.

overallFeedback.feedback: The key reason is that organism identification (culture, Gram stain, serology) is unavailable or impractical at the point of care in most Indian settings. Syndromic management bypasses this by treating all probable pathogens of the presenting syndrome.

Exactly. The syndromic approach was born from the reality that in resource-limited Indian primary care, laboratory diagnosis is unavailable, delayed, or lost to follow-up — so treatment targets the syndrome, covering all likely causative organisms at once.

interactions.label: Using the clinical framework for rapid triage of genital ulcers, which pair of c

params.question: Using the clinical framework for rapid triage of genital ulcers, which pair of conditions presents with PAINFUL ulcers?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Both syphilis (painless indurated chancre) and LGV (transient, often-unnoticed painless ulcer) fall on the PAINLESS side of the framework.

Correct. Chancroid produces a painful, soft, ragged ulcer and herpes genitalis presents as painful grouped vesicles that rupture into shallow ulcers — both are on the painful side of the triage framework.
Donovanosis produces a painless, beefy-red, friable ulcer. Only chancroid is painful in this pair.
While herpes is painful, donovanosis is characteristically painless (beefy-red granulation tissue). They fall on opposite sides of the framework.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember the framework: PAINFUL ulcers = chancroid (soft, ragged, undermined edges) and herpes genitalis (grouped vesicles → shallow ulcers). PAINLESS ulcers = syphilis (indurated chancre), LGV, and donovanosis.

The painful-versus-painless question is the single highest-yield first move in genital ulcer triage: painful ulcers point to chancroid or herpes; painless ulcers point to syphilis, LGV, or donovanosis.

interactions.label: A patient diagnosed with late latent syphilis of unknown duration and no neurolo

params.question: A patient diagnosed with late latent syphilis of unknown duration and no neurological involvement presents for treatment. What is the correct benzathine penicillin G regimen?

answers.text: A single dose of 2.4 million units intramuscularly

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: A single IM dose is the regimen for early syphilis (primary, secondary, or early latent within 2 years). Late latent disease requires a longer course to address the slower, lower-burden infection.

answers.text: 2.4 million units intramuscularly weekly for three doses (total 7.2 MU)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Late latent syphilis, latent syphilis of unknown duration, and non-neurological tertiary syphilis require 3 weekly IM injections of 2.4 MU benzathine penicillin G, totalling 7.2 million units.

answers.text: Aqueous crystalline penicillin G 3–4 MU intravenously every 4 hours for 10–14 days

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This IV regimen is reserved specifically for neurosyphilis, where adequate CSF penetration is critical. The question specifies no neurological involvement.

answers.text: 2.4 million units intramuscularly weekly for two doses (total 4.8 MU)

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: There is no two-dose regimen in standard syphilis treatment. Early syphilis needs one dose; late latent/tertiary (non-neuro) needs three weekly doses.

overallFeedback.feedback: The core principle is stage-based dosing: early syphilis (primary/secondary/early latent) gets a single IM dose of 2.4 MU; late latent or tertiary (without neurological involvement) gets 2.4 MU IM weekly × 3 doses; neurosyphilis requires IV aqueous crystalline penicillin.

Correct. The staging principle is: early syphilis = 1 dose IM; late latent or tertiary (non-neuro) = 3 weekly doses IM; neurosyphilis = IV crystalline penicillin. Always match the regimen to the stage.

interactions.label: Which complication can result from untreated gonococcal or chlamydial urethritis

params.question: Which complication can result from untreated gonococcal or chlamydial urethritis in men?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: PID is the ascending complication in women, not men. In women, untreated cervicitis can ascend to the fallopian tubes and peritoneum.
Correct. In men, untreated urethral infection can ascend to cause epididymo-orchitis — inflammation of the epididymis and testis — which may impair fertility if untreated.
Bartholin's gland is a female anatomical structure. Its infection is unrelated to ascending urethritis in men.
Cervical ectopy is a condition of the uterine cervix and is not a complication of male urethritis.

overallFeedback.feedback: In men, untreated urethritis (gonococcal or chlamydial) can ascend to cause epididymo-orchitis. In women, the corresponding ascending complication is pelvic inflammatory disease. Recognising and treating the urethral discharge syndrome early prevents these sequelae.
Epididymo-orchitis is the key ascending complication of untreated gonococcal/chlamydial urethritis in men, which is why prompt syndromic treatment matters — the patient may not return.

interactions.label: A 28-year-old man is treated for urethral discharge at your STI clinic. You hand

params.question: A 28-year-old man is treated for urethral discharge at your STI clinic. You hand him a contact slip to give to his recent sexual partners. Which component of the '4 Cs' does this action primarily address?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Compliance refers to ensuring the index patient completes the full course of prescribed treatment. The contact slip is not about medication adherence.
Counselling covers education on safe sexual behaviour, condom use, and why partners need treatment. While related, the specific act of giving a contact slip is the mechanism for a different C.

Correct. The contact-slip method is the operational tool for contact tracing — it invites recent sexual partners to attend for evaluation and presumptive treatment without identifying the index patient, thereby breaking the transmission chain.
The condom component refers to promoting consistent barrier use to prevent future transmission. The contact slip addresses reaching partners already exposed.

overallFeedback.feedback: The 4 Cs are: Contact tracing (reaching exposed partners — the contact slip is its tool), Counselling (education on safe behaviour), Compliance (completing the treatment course), and Condoms (consistent barrier use). The contact slip directly operationalises contact tracing.

The contact slip is the practical mechanism for contact tracing — one of the 4 Cs (Contact tracing, Counselling, Compliance, Condoms). It breaks the transmission chain by reaching exposed partners anonymously.
